title: The Private Ghostwriter
pitch: Combine Humanizer's AI-tell-removal skill with Magnitude's fully local model hosting to build an offline writing assistant for people who legally or ethically can't send their drafts to a cloud API: lawyers polishing client letters, journalists protecting sources, therapists writing case notes, or students who don't trust 'AI detector' privacy policies. The pitch: everything runs on the user's own laptop, so a paralegal can draft a demand letter with AI help and have it read naturally, with zero data ever leaving the machine and no subscription to an OpenAI-style API. Sell it as a one-time-purchase desktop app rather than a subscription, since the target buyer already distrusts recurring cloud services.
why_now: AI-detection anxiety and data-privacy rules (client confidentiality, GDPR, HIPAA-adjacent concerns) are pushing professionals toward on-device AI at the same time 'sounds like AI' has become a real reputational risk in writing — this mashup lands right at that intersection.
